title: Duplicate Checkout Requests
business_scenario: Customer double-clicks the Place Order button or submits checkout multiple times during network latency.
symptoms: Multiple distinct orders are placed with the same cart items, charging the customer multiple times and double-decrementing stock.
reproduction_steps: Send two simultaneous POST requests to /api/checkout/place-order with identical cart state or rapid clicks.
expected_behavior: Only one valid checkout operation should be accepted for the same checkout attempt. Duplicate submissions should be rejected with 409 Conflict or return the existing completed order.
actual_behavior: Both requests proceed simultaneously and generate duplicate order records (e.g. ord-1 and ord-2).
root_cause: Absence of an idempotency key verification and lack of a critical concurrency lock on the user's active checkout session in checkout.service.js.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent requests with the same checkout context must result in exactly 1 created order, with the second request either rejected with 409 or returning the original order.
reference_fix: Enforce in-flight mutex locking keyed by userId and verify idempotency tokens cached upon initial order completion in checkout.service.js.
regression_tests: Single checkout successfully places order and clears cart.
Subsequent checkout with fresh cart proceeds normally.
